coverage_note: 14:09-24:00 drill on et2assaf is mostly '[speaking Arabic]/[speaking foreign language]' - his Arabic lost; rows at 21:07 and 22:14 rebuilt from Amal's lines (low). 27:46-1:03:46 Medi and much of Amal are Latin-transliterated by the engine; shadda (doubled middle) is invisible, so ba5arreb/ba5rab slips only filed where Amal voiced them. Names amrica/Amal not flagged. Pronunciation (behtr, ma tarat, stawarini) and self-fixes (sab3teen, yom el-sabt, blouzeti) left out.

rows.why: He said 'they have' about his own shop; Amal recast to 3indna (we have) and her chat wrote 3indna.
rows.english: We had a lot of customers.

rows.medi_said: أنا لا بعرف، بتعرف في Jambalaya؟
rows.why: Verb negated with la (fus7a) instead of ma; Amal let it pass (best reading ma ba3ref).
rows.english: I don't know, do you know jambalaya?

rows.medi_said: أنا لا بعرف، بتعرف في Jambalaya؟
rows.why: Asking Amal (a woman) 'do you know' with the masculine you-form; best reading bte3refi.

rows.medi_said: is أكل من الـ جنوب أمريكي،
rows.why: el- on the first word of 'south of America'; her chat (context only) wrote janoob amrica with no el-.
rows.english: It's food from the American South.

rows.medi_said: عنده ماي بس، uh، uh، فيها ماي بس شوي
rows.why: Used 3ind (has) for 'there is water in it'; Amal said 'fiha, not 3indha' (he had half self-fixed in the same turn, but she voiced it).
Non-word / wrong word for 'light, thin'; Amal supplied 5afeef and her chat wrote it.
rows.english: It has a little water, light.

rows.why: Apology said with a non-word; sheet: 'sorry | aasef | آسف'. Best reading, Amal let it pass.
He reached for the word for sausage and produced sijal; Amal supplied سجق and her chat wrote sujo2.

rows.medi_said: و، و، uh، daiman behtr، um, sos behtr.
rows.why: Habitual 'always is' needs bikoon; Amal recast daiman beykoon and he repeated it (Daiman bykon).
rows.english: And the sauce is always spicy.

rows.medi_said: ما بحب، ما بحب eat sausage.
rows.why: English 'eat' inside an Arabic sentence; sheet: 'eat | Kul | كل'. Pre-ruled AR-1933 do not correct.

rows.amal_said: مش صحي لا، ومش عشان مش صحي.
rows.why: Said sa7ee7 (correct/true) for 'healthy'; Amal recast se7i. Sheet: 'healthy | Se77i | صحي'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, be-- Or it's feminine. بتبدأ.
rows.amal_said: شو بتبدأ؟ ... It starts cold يعني؟
rows.why: Present 'it starts' for 'the cold has started'; Amal queried it and confirmed past, then gave بدا.
Feminine -at on bada with masculine jaw; Amal said bada and explained 'here you're saying جو so it has to be masculine'.
Letters swapped (daba for bada), the same slip the brief cites from 09-26; Amal said بدا twice.
Amal recast with el-: el-dunya.

rows.amal_said: No, no, no. Either دنيا or جو. One just one.
rows.why: He stacked both weather subjects; Amal said explicitly use one.
rows.proposed_rule: For weather, the subject is either el-dunya (feminine) or el-jaw (masculine), never both together: el-dunya bardi / el-jaw baared.

rows.why: dunya is feminine (Amal just said so) but adjective left masculine, and el- dropped again; she let it pass.
Wrong word for 'cloudy'; Amal supplied m8ayyme.

rows.medi_said: بس، um، في المدينة الأول مطر.
rows.why: awwal + noun takes no el- (like a7la matar, which Amal had just modelled); she let it pass.
rows.english: But in the city, the first rain...

rows.amal_said: آه غبرة. ... We didn't learn dust.
rows.why: Used zbaale (garbage) for 'dust'; Amal supplied 8abra and said they had not learned it, so a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: uh, زرقا و pantalon بيج وكندرة بنية.
rows.why: French/Farsi form of the word; sheet: 'pants | Ban6aloan | بنطلون'. Amal let it pass.
rows.english: Blue blouse, beige pants and brown shoes.

rows.medi_said: أنا راح أعمله بس الـ زباين،
rows.amal_said: إنت كنت راح تعمله. ... كنت راح تعمله.
rows.chat: kunet ra7 = I was going to
rows.why: 'I was going to do it' needs kunt before ra7; Amal recast twice and chatted 'kunet ra7 = I was going to'.
rows.english: I was going to do it but the customers...

rows.why: Wrong form for 'in a hurry'; sheet: 'in a hurry / rushed | Mista3jel | مستعجل'. Best reading, she let it pass.
rows.english: The customers are in a hurry.

rows.amal_said: شي غلط. بس one note إنه عم، عم بعمل is internal clipping, so what's he made? عمل.
rows.why: His words were lost to the engine; Amal named the rule (internal clipping, 3emel = he made) for the past of 3amal in 'if he did something wrong'.
rows.english: He always apologizes if he did something wrong.

rows.why: His Arabic lost; Amal prompted 'All كل' for 'everyone' and then explained kul 7ada vs el-kul, chat lalkul.
His Arabic lost; Amal voiced tet2assafi (bare verb after laazem, feminine) as the fix.

rows.amal_said: to you. ... So the full verb.
rows.why: 'to you' given as illi (to me); Amal prompted 'to you' and he fixed it to fillik, she said صح.

rows.amal_said: No, no على عندك. Just either على or عند.
rows.why: Stacked two prepositions; Amal said use either 3ala beitek or 3indek, he fixed to andik.
rows.english: Because I can't go to your place.

rows.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] is I ruin or I make not work.
rows.wrong: I ruin or I make not work
rows.right: I am ruined / it gets ruined
rows.why: He glossed ba5rab (get ruined) as the causative; Amal said No and he fixed it.
rows.english: ba5rab = I get ruined; ba5arreb = I ruin something.

rows.medi_said: because of the kam, but there's a khutat,
rows.amal_said: الـ cam only bring it back to singular.
rows.why: Plural after kam; Amal named the rule and he said kam khuta, ممتاز.
rows.english: How many plans have you ruined?

rows.amal_said: خرّبتي أو خرّبت. ... No، خرّب، بـ-بخرب is the internal flipping. بخرّب is not.
rows.why: Used the get-ruined verb (5ereb) for 'you ruined'; Amal recast the doubled 5arrabti and said No to kharabit.
rows.english: How many plans have you ruined?

rows.why: Object fronted (the plans you ruined) so the verb needs the pointer -hom; Amal prompted هم and he added it.
rows.english: The plans you ruined were mine.

rows.why: Feminine singular kaanat for plural plans; Amal recast kaanu and explained 5u6a6 is plural.

rows.medi_said: بيصلع-- بيصلح كل، كل إشي اللي، uh, بيخربه.
rows.amal_said: ما في كل إشي في الجملة. Not everything just what. so اللي بيخربه.
rows.why: 'what he breaks' is illi alone; kul ishi illi adds 'everything' (redundant); Amal said so explicitly.
rows.english: He usually fixes what he breaks.

rows.why: Non-word for 'I broke it'; Amal supplied the verb 5arrab. Engine may have misheard.

rows.medi_said: kharabt kom, kharabt kom, kharabet kom.
rows.why: Object ending -kom (you pl) for 'them'; Amal recast 5arrabthom and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: We never broke it tie. Break it.
rows.why: Past tense for a present habit 'we never break it'; Amal prompted 'Break it' and he switched to ma ban kharab.

rows.medi_said: lama haket ziyada, ziyada ana, uh, kharab kul shee.
rows.why: 'I ruin/ruined everything' with the he-form (and the get-ruined verb); Amal let it pass and gave an idiom instead.
rows.english: When I talked too much, I ruined everything.

rows.why: 'my fiancee uses' needs the she-form test3mel, he used the you-fem form; Amal recast Istamel.
rows.english: When my fiancee uses my computer...

rows.why: 'it was funny' needs the doubled make-laugh form; Amal recast and asked what bida77ek means, he was confused.

rows.amal_said: Do you get happy? This is-- This means do you get happy? ... Inti mabsuta?
rows.why: Verb 'do you get happy' for 'are you happy'; Amal said it means do you get happy and gave mabsuta.

rows.amal_said: Ma dun-- bidun be. So ma tkun.
rows.why: Negative command needs ma + you-form (ma tkun), not ma bikun; Amal recast.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, ma tadaitni. Ma ta- ma tadait.
rows.why: 'don't get upset with me' takes min (minni), not an object -ni; Amal recast and he said 'You have to add min'.
'Don't upset me' is the doubled causative without t-; Amal recast twice, he still repeated tadaitni.
Command takes no t- prefix; Amal said 'No t bas ghayiri'.
'Don't hurt me' given as a positive command; Amal prompted Ma and he fixed to ma tawazayini.
